chill.title: Morning quiet in the Blue Mosque courtyard
chill.description: Arrive before the tour groups and sit in the marble courtyard with the fountain at the center — this is what stillness looks like.
chill.bonus: Arrive at or before 8am. You'll have it almost to yourself.

chill.title: Tea at Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medresesi çayhane, Beyazıt
chill.description: A Turkish tea house costs almost nothing and gives you a front-row seat to the whole city — order a third tea and let the afternoon dissolve.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone face-down the whole time.

chill.title: Golden-hour cruise on Şehir Hatları Bosphorus ferry
chill.description: Take the public ferry from Eminönü up the Bosphorus as the light goes golden — minarets, bridges, and tankers all at once for a few lira.
chill.bonus: Sit on the upper deck. No headphones.

chill.title: Explore the Princes' Islands by bicycle
chill.description: An hour's ferry ride from Istanbul lies a car-free island where horse-drawn carriages and bicycles rule — Büyükada is a perfect day outside the city.
chill.bonus: Swim in the Marmara Sea before you take the ferry back.

chill.title: Wander the painted houses of Balat
chill.description: Balat's cobblestone streets and faded Ottoman townhouses are one of Istanbul's great free pleasures — just walk without a map.
chill.bonus: Get genuinely lost and don't check your phone for 30 minutes.

chill.title: Browse the Istanbul Book Bazaar
chill.description: Sahaflar Çarşısı behind the Grand Bazaar sells Ottoman manuscripts, vintage maps, and secondhand novels — two hours will feel like twenty minutes.
chill.bonus: Leave with something you didn't expect to buy.

chill.title: Sunset on the Walls at Yedikule Fortress
chill.description: Walk the surviving stretch of Theodosian land walls at Yedikule as the sun drops behind the Marmara and the city dims to amber — almost nobody is here.
chill.bonus: Climb to the highest accessible tower and stay until the first star appears — name it.

chill.title: Tea Garden at Pierre Loti Café, Eyüp
chill.description: Perched on a hilltop above the Golden Horn in a neighbourhood most tourists never reach, Pierre Loti serves çay with a panorama that stops time.
chill.bonus: Take the cable car up and walk the cemetery path down through the Ottoman tombstones — read one inscription aloud.

chill.title: Hammam Soak at Çemberlitaş Hamamı
chill.description: A 1584 Sinan-designed hammam in the heart of the old city scrubs four centuries of travelers and today it scrubs you on the same heated marble slab.
chill.bonus: Request the full kese scrub and kil soap massage — don't flinch when the tellak wrings the foam sack over your face.

adventure.title: Hike the Belgrad Forest trails
adventure.description: A vast Ottoman reservoir forest 20km north of the city — get on a minibus, get off, and walk among 500-year-old dams with almost nobody around.
adventure.bonus: Walk to the farthest reservoir and back without a trail app.

adventure.title: Sprint through the Grand Bazaar finding all gates
adventure.description: The Grand Bazaar has 61 covered streets and 22 entrances — pick a gate, exit it, circle the outside, find the next gate, repeat until you've done them all.
adventure.bonus: Count the gates as you go. The number at the end is your score.

adventure.title: Explore the Basilica Cistern underground
adventure.description: A 6th-century underground reservoir built by Justinian — 336 marble columns rising from black water in permanent dim light, with a Medusa head at the corner.
adventure.bonus: Find both Medusa column bases. One is upside down, one is sideways.

adventure.title: Paraglide over the Bosphorus from the Asian side
adventure.description: Launch from Büyük Çamlıca Hill with the city at your feet, two seas visible, and the bridge connecting them — this is what Istanbul looks like from the air.
adventure.bonus: Count the minarets you can see from altitude. There are a lot.

adventure.title: Kayak the upper Bosphorus between continents
adventure.description: Rent a sea kayak from the Rumeli side and paddle between Europe and Asia while tankers ghost past you — technically the same waterway, technically two worlds.
adventure.bonus: Touch the Asian shore. You've now kayaked between continents.

adventure.title: Take the morning ferry to Asia and walk back
adventure.description: Catch the first ferry to the Asian side, walk the Kadıköy market, eat breakfast, then take the bridge back on foot — two continents before noon.
adventure.bonus: Don't plan the route. Just follow your feet.

adventure.title: Night Ferry to Kadıköy Alone
adventure.description: The late Şehir Hatları ferry crosses the Bosphorus after midnight when the city lights smear on the water and the deck is yours.
adventure.bonus: Stand at the very bow of the upper deck and don't hold the railing for the full crossing.

adventure.title: Rooftop Paragliding Launch from Büyükada
adventure.description: The largest of the Princes' Islands drops away beneath you as you launch over the Marmara Sea with no cars, no noise, just salt air and altitude.
adventure.bonus: Ask the pilot to fly you directly over the Greek Orthodox Orphanage ruins and take one photo mid-flight.

adventure.title: Bosphorus Strait Swim at Kız Kulesi
adventure.description: You swim one of the world's great waterways where Europe and Asia nearly touch, with tankers and ferries cutting the horizon.
adventure.bonus: Touch the Asian shore and the European shore on the same day — document both with a wet hand on the wall.

foodie.title: Kebap dinner at Hamdi Restaurant, Eminönü
foodie.description: Doner over bread drowned in tomato sauce and hot butter — find the Istanbul outpost of the restaurant that invented it and pay your respects.
foodie.bonus: Eat every last drop of the sauce with bread. Don't you dare leave it.

foodie.title: Baklava tasting at Karaköy Güllüoğlu
foodie.description: Work through at least four varieties — pistachio, walnut, fıstıklı, sütlü — and drink the strong tea they push without asking.
foodie.bonus: Pick one to bring back for someone else.

foodie.title: Lahmacun at Bafra Pidecisi, Karaköy
foodie.description: The thin, crispy Turkish flatbread topped with spiced lamb is a one-dollar meal that earns its own pilgrimage.
foodie.bonus: Roll it up, squeeze lemon over it, and eat walking.

foodie.title: Kokoreç at Meşhur Beşiktaş Kokoreçcisi
foodie.description: Order the seasoned lamb intestine sandwich from the most smoke-blackened cart you can find — this is not the time for caution.
foodie.bonus: Order double and eat standing up without a napkin.

foodie.title: Stuffed mussels from the midyecis of Rüstempaşa, Eminönü
foodie.description: Midye dolma vendors haul trays of stuffed mussels along the waterfront — eat them one after another until you run out of lemon.
foodie.bonus: Count how many you eat and try to beat it next time.

foodie.title: Dinner at Barba Restaurant, Balat
foodie.description: Eat among faded mansions and minarets as the Golden Horn turns gold beneath you — Balat's rooftop restaurants deliver this for cheap.
foodie.bonus: Stay until the first call to prayer after dark.

foodie.title: Meyhane Crawl on Nevizade Sokak
foodie.description: This narrow alley off İstiklal packs a dozen meyhanes shoulder to shoulder, each with live fasıl music and bottomless meze until the small hours.
foodie.bonus: Hit at least three different meyhanes and order rakı with a meze at each — finish every glass.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Mikla, Beyoğlu
foodie.description: Chef Mehmet Gürs reimagines Anatolian ingredients on the rooftop of the Marmara Pera hotel with the whole Istanbul skyline as the backdrop.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair each course with only Turkish wine — no exceptions, even if they push back.

foodie.title: Balık Ekmek from a Galata Bridge Boat
foodie.description: A grilled mackerel sandwich slapped together on a rocking boat moored under Galata Bridge is one of Istanbul's purest street food experiences.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing on the bridge while a fisherman casts directly beside you — don't move for the whole sandwich.

foodie.title: Breakfast Spread at Van Kahvaltı Evi, Cihangir
foodie.description: This Kurdish breakfast institution in Cihangir drowns your table in forty small plates of cheese, honey, clotted cream, and herbs before 11am.
foodie.bonus: Order çay refills until the waiter stops counting — try to hit seven glasses in one sitting.

social.title: Nargile session at a Tophane café
social.description: Tophane's waterfront nargile cafés are an institution — order double-apple, recline, and watch ferries cross the Bosphorus all evening.
social.bonus: Go with someone you've been meaning to have a long conversation with.

social.title: Rooftop drinks at Neolokal, SALT Galata
social.description: The Bosphorus turns molten at dusk — there are a dozen rooftop bars in Beyoğlu that cost nothing to sit in and everything to leave.
social.bonus: Stay for the first lights across the water.

social.title: Whirling dervish ceremony at a tekke
social.description: A Sema ceremony is not a tourist show — it's a Sufi meditation in motion, and sitting in silence watching it rearranges something in your chest.

social.title: Backgammon at a çay bahçesi in Üsküdar
social.description: Cross to the Asian side, find a tea garden full of old men, and challenge someone to a game — no shared language required.
social.bonus: Lose gracefully and order the next round of tea.

social.title: Gallery crawl in Karaköy and Galata
social.description: The compact blocks between Karaköy and the Galata Tower are dense with contemporary art spaces, many free and unexpected.
social.bonus: Find one piece you'd actually hang at home and photograph it.

social.title: Grand Bazaar treasure hunt with a budget
social.description: Set a 200 TL budget, enter at one gate, and don't leave until you've spent it all on something you didn't know you needed.
social.bonus: Negotiate on at least two items. Refuse the first price every time.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at 360 Istanbul
social.description: 360 wraps the top floor of a building on İstiklal with a panoramic terrace that puts both bridges, both shores, and the entire Bosphorus in one eyeful.
social.bonus: Point out and name every landmark visible from the terrace to whoever you're with — Google nothing.

social.title: Backgammon at a Kıraathane in Fatih
social.description: The old coffee houses of Fatih are strictly local — men play tavla over çay for hours and a foreigner pulling up a stool is the most interesting thing to happen all week.
social.bonus: Challenge someone to a game using only hand gestures — no translation apps allowed.

social.title: Beşiktaş Match at Vodafone Park
social.description: Vodafone Park is one of Europe's loudest stadiums when Beşiktaş play at home and the Çarşı ultras section turns the whole harbor side of the city into a drum.
social.bonus: Learn the main Çarşı chant phonetically before kick-off and sing it in the stands — loudly, from the first minute.

social.title: Rakı Night at Münferit, Beyoğlu
social.description: Münferit is a convivial modern meyhane on Yeniçarşı Caddesi that attracts Istanbul's creative crowd for long evenings of rakı, meze, and uninhibited conversation.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to the table next to you within the first twenty minutes and get a restaurant recommendation from them before you leave.

active.title: Stand-up paddleboard on Büyükçekmece Lake
active.description: A vast calm lagoon west of the city with SUP rentals, almost no crowds, and a 16th-century Suleiman bridge watching over the whole scene.
active.bonus: Paddle to the Ottoman bridge and touch it.

active.title: Row a boat in the Sweet Waters of Asia
active.description: Göksu Deresi, the Sweet Waters of Asia, is a reed-lined river where locals have picnicked for centuries — rent a rowboat and float through it.
active.bonus: Stop rowing. Drift. See where you end up.

active.title: Walk the full length of İstiklal Caddesi to the tower
active.description: The 1.4km pedestrian boulevard from Taksim to Galata Tower hums at all hours — do it end to end, then climb the tower for the view.
active.bonus: Count the side streets you want to come back to.

active.title: Cycle the Princes' Islands perimeter
active.description: Büyükada's car-free perimeter road is a 10km loop through pine forest, Ottoman villas, and sea views — rent a bike off the ferry and ride the whole thing.
active.bonus: Stop at the highest point and look back at Istanbul across the water.

active.title: Swim at Kilyos Black Sea beach
active.description: Take the bus north through the Belgrade Forest and hit the Black Sea — Kilyos is rough, cold, and perfect, with almost no tourists.
active.bonus: Go in the water first, ask questions later.

active.title: Climb Çamlıca Hill for 360° city panorama
active.description: Istanbul's highest point on the Asian side rewards a 30-minute hike with the full city skyline, both bridges, and two seas all at once.
active.bonus: Identify both bridges and both seas from the top.

active.title: Climb the Galata Tower Stairs, Then Run to Karaköy
active.description: Skip the elevator at Galata Tower, take all 146 steps to the top, then sprint the steep cobbled descent to the Karaköy waterfront before your legs give out.
active.bonus: Time yourself from the tower base to the ferry terminal pier — beat twelve minutes.

active.title: Sea Kayaking the Golden Horn with Boğaziçi Outdoor
active.description: Boğaziçi Outdoor launches kayaks from Ayvansaray and paddles you through the Golden Horn with Byzantine walls and Ottoman mosques towering on both banks.
active.bonus: Paddle close enough to touch the base of the Ayvansaray sea walls without grounding the kayak.

active.title: Dawn Run Across the Bosphorus Bridge
active.description: On race days the FSM Bridge closes to cars and runners own six kilometers of elevated highway over the strait — join the Vodafone 15K or show up for an open training run.
active.bonus: Stop exactly at the bridge midpoint, straddle the continental divide marker, and do ten jumping jacks over two continents.
